S1_comparative_drug_efficacy.synthesis: Evidence from randomized controlled trials and network meta-analyses indicates that both SGLT2 inhibitors and GLP-1 receptor agonists provide substantial cardiorenal protection in patients with type 2 diabetes and chronic kidney disease, but exhibit distinct profile advantages. Empagliflozin significantly reduces progression of kidney disease and cardiovascular death (hazard ratio 0.72) [PMID: 35100001]. Once-weekly semaglutide reduces major adverse cardiovascular events (hazard ratio 0.74) and diabetic nephropathy [PMID: 35100002]. In direct network meta-analysis, SGLT2 inhibitors were superior in preventing heart failure hospitalization (RR 0.68 vs 0.90) and end-stage kidney disease, whereas GLP-1 receptor agonists achieved greater stroke reduction (RR 0.85 vs 0.99) [PMID: 35100003].

S2_rare_disease_crag_corrective.synthesis: While sotorasib demonstrates significant progression-free survival benefits over docetaxel in KRAS G12C-mutated advanced NSCLC [PMID: 35200001], acquired resistance universally develops. Genomic profiling demonstrates that resistance is mediated by secondary KRAS switch II mutations such as Y96D, A59S, and Q61H, as well as bypass RTK activation [PMID: 35200002]. High-level MET gene amplification occurs in approximately 13-14% of progressing patients, restoring downstream MAPK and PI3K/mTOR cascades [PMID: 35200004]. Co-targeting with SHP2 inhibitors or MET inhibitors overcomes this resistance in preclinical models [PMID: 35200005].

S3_corpus_absence_abstention.synthesis: There is insufficient scientific evidence to support the efficacy of hyperbaric oxygen therapy in reversing advanced Stage IV tau aggregation in Alzheimer's disease. Experimental models of advanced tauopathy demonstrate that hyperbaric oxygenation fails to reduce insoluble hyperphosphorylated tau levels or reverse neurofibrillary tangles (tau pS396/total tau ratio 1.04 vs 0.99; p = 0.78) [PMID: 35500005]. No human clinical trials validate pathological tau clearance with hyperbaric therapy. The system abstains from claiming clinical benefit due to absent therapeutic evidence.

S4_strict_temporal_study_type_filter.synthesis: Randomized controlled trials published after 2022 establish that mRNA vaccines provide robust immunogenicity and protection in pediatric cohorts. In children aged 6 months to 4 years, a three-dose series of BNT162b2 showed 73.2% efficacy with favorable reactogenicity [PMID: 35300001]. Similarly, two 25-ug doses of mRNA-1273 demonstrated noninferior neutralizing antibody titers and prevented symptomatic infection in young children [PMID: 35300002]. In immunocompromised pediatric recipients, bivalent mRNA boosters generated 4.3-fold higher neutralizing titers [PMID: 35300004]. Furthermore, a Phase 3 trial of an investigational pediatric mRNA RSV vaccine in infants demonstrated 81.4% efficacy against lower respiratory tract disease [PMID: 35300005].

S5_lay_query_acronym_normalization.synthesis: Long-term evidence confirms that metformin monotherapy provides durable reduction in myocardial infarction risk among patients with type 2 diabetes. In the 10-year post-trial follow-up of the UKPDS, intensive glucose control with metformin conferred a 33% reduction in myocardial infarction risk (hazard ratio 0.67; p = 0.005) and a 27% reduction in all-cause mortality [PMID: 35600001]. In older adults, initiating metformin was associated with a 20% lower hazard of composite cardiovascular events compared with sulfonylurea monotherapy (adjusted HR 0.80) [PMID: 35600002].
